paragraphs.sourceText: In the center of a big city there are usually dozens of large office buildings that house big banks, corporation headquarters, and government agencies. Thousands of people work in these buildings. People who do all the office work are called white-collar workers. 26 and receptionists, bookkeepers and computer operators work for many different kinds of companies.

Many office workers dream of working their way up to the top, from clerk to 27 of a corporation. The way lies through middle management. Middle management includes junior executives, who may fill 28 jobs, supervise other workers in the company, 29 action to top management, or see that the company’s policies are 30 .At the very top are the senior executives. They 31 the policies for their own companies, especially 32 .The Chief Executive Officer, or CEO, of a large 33 has a great deal of power and influence.

It is believed that one can start out at the bottom and go all the way to the top. Because financial matters are so important, some accountants become top executives. In companies where technology is important, people with an engineering background can also rise to the top. Nowadays, however, education 34 in the selection of people for management jobs. Universities in many countries offer courses in business administration. The graduates of these courses often start out in middle management jobs. From there, they can easily get promoted if they show the necessary 35 and ability.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 36 to 45 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 36 至 45 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: For decades, Americans have taken for granted the United States’ leadership position in the development of new technologies. The innovations (创新）that resulted from research and development during World War Ⅱand afterwards were 36 to the prosperity of the nation in the second half of the 20th century. Those innovations, upon which virtually all aspects of 37 society now depend, were possible because the United States then 38 the world in mathematics and science education. Today, however, despite increasing demand for workers with strong skills in mathematics and science, the 39 of degrees awarded in science, math, and engineering are decreasing.

The decline in degree production in what are called the STEM disciplines (science, technology, engineering, and math) seems to be 40 related to the comparatively weak performance by US schoolchildren on international assessments of math and science. Many students entering college have weak skills in mathematics. According to the 2005 report of the Business-Higher Education Forum, 22 percent of college freshmen must take remedial(补习的）math 41 , and less than half of the students who plan to major in science or engineering 42 complete a major in those fields.

The result has been a decrease in the number of American college graduates who have the skills, 43 in mathematics, to power a workforce that can keep the country at the forefront（前沿）of innovation and maintain its standard of living. With the 44 performance of American students in math and science has come increased competition from students from other countries that have strongly supported education in these areas. Many more students earn 45 in the STEM disciplines in developing countries than in the United States.

Directions ：In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. Ban Sugary Drinks—That Will Add Fuel to the Obesity War
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。禁止含糖饮料——这将为肥胖战争火上浇油

paragraphs.sourceText: A) On a train last Thursday, I sat opposite a man who was so fat he filled more than one seat. He was pale and disfigured and looked sick to death, which he probably was: obesity (肥胖症）leads to many nasty ways of dying. Looking around the carriage, I saw quite a few people like him, including a couple of fatty children with swollen cheeks pressing against their eyes. These people are part of what is without exaggeration an epidemic (流行病) of obesity.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 上周四在火车上，我坐在一个男人对面，他太胖了，以至于占据了不止一个座位。他脸色苍白，毁容，看上去病得要死，大概就是这样：肥胖会导致很多令人讨厌的死法。环顾车厢，我看到像他这样的人不少，其中有几个胖胖的孩子，脸颊肿得贴着眼睛。这些人毫不夸张地说是肥胖流行病的一部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) But it is quite unnecessary: there is a simple idea—far from new—that could spare millions of such people a lifetime of chronic(长期的）ill health, and at the same time save the National Health Service(NHS) at least￡14 billion a year in England and Wales. There would, you might think, be considerable public interest in it. This simple idea is that sugar is as good—or as bad—as poison and should be avoided. It is pure, white and deadly, as Professor John Yudkin described it 40 years ago in a revolutionary book of that name. The subtitle was How Sugar Is Killing Us.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 但这是完全没有必要的：有一个简单的想法——远非新鲜事——可以让数以百万计的此类人终生免受慢性（长期的）健康不良的困扰，同时在英格兰和威尔士每年为国家医疗服务体系（NHS）节省至少140亿英镑。你可能会认为，公众对此有相当大的兴趣。这个简单的想法是糖与毒药一样好——或一样坏——应该避免。正如约翰·尤德金教授所描述的那样，糖是纯净的、白色的和致命的。 40 年前，在一本同名的革命性书籍中，副标题是“糖如何杀死我们”。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) In its countless hidden forms, in ready meals, junk food and sweet drinks, sugar leads to addiction (癮）,to hormonal upsets to the appetite, to metabolic (新陈代谢的）malfunctions and obesity and from there to type 2 diabetes (糖尿病) and its many horrible complications. If people really grasped that, they would try to kick the habit, particularly as Britain is the “fat man of Europe”. They might even feel driven to support government measures to prevent people from consuming this deadly stuff. Yet so far this idea has met little but resistance.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 以无数隐藏的形式，在即食食品、垃圾食品和甜饮料中，糖会导致成瘾（瘾）、荷尔蒙失调、食欲紊乱、代谢功能障碍和肥胖，进而导致 2 型糖尿病（糖尿病）及其许多可怕的并发症。如果人们真正认识到这一点，他们会尝试戒掉这个习惯，特别是因为英国是“欧洲胖子”。他们甚至可能会感到有动力支持政府采取措施，防止人们食用这种致命的东西。但到目前为止，这个想法除了阻力之外，几乎没有遇到什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) It is not difficult to imagine the vested interests (既得利益集团）lined up against any sugar control—all the food and drink manufacturers, processors, promoters and retailers who make such easy pickings out of the magic powers of sugar. Then there are the liberals, with whom I would normally side, who protest that government regulation would be yet another instance of interference in our lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）不难想象，既得利益集团会联合起来反对任何糖类管制——所有食品和饮料制造商、加工商、促销员和零售商都如此轻易地利用了糖的魔力。然后是自由主义者，我通常会站在他们一边，他们抗议政府监管将是干预我们生活的又一个例子。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) That is true, but people should realise that you cannot have a welfare state without a nanny state (保姆国家）,to some degree. If we are all to be responsible for one another’s health insurance, through socialised medicine, then we are all closely involved in one another^ health, including everyone’s eating and drinking. That has already been admitted, finally, with smoking. But it has yet to be admitted with overeating, even though one in four adults in this country is obese and that number is predicted to double by the year 2050. Quite apart from anything else, obesity will cripple the NHS.
paragraphs.translationZh: E）确实如此，但人们应该认识到，在某种程度上，没有保姆国家就不可能有福利国家。如果我们都通过社会化医疗为彼此的健康保险负责，那么我们都密切参与彼此的健康，包括每个人的饮食。最后，吸烟已经承认了这一点。但暴饮暴食尚未得到承认，尽管这个国家有四分之一的成年人肥胖，而且这个数字预计到今年会翻一番2050 年。不说别的，肥胖将削弱国民医疗服务体系 (NHS)。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Recently, though, there have been signs that the medical establishment is trying to sound the alarm. Last month the Academy of Medical Royal Colleges (AMRC) published a report saying that obesity is the greatest public health issue affecting the UK and urging government to do something.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 不过，最近有迹象表明医疗机构正试图拉响警报。上个月，英国皇家医学院（AMRC）发布了一份报告，称肥胖是影响英国的最大公共卫生问题，并敦促政府采取行动。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) The report offers 10 recommendations, of which the first is imposing a tax of 20 percent on sugary drinks for at least a year, on top of the existing 20 percent value-added tax. That at least would be an excellent start. The amounts of sugar in soft drinks are horrifying, and turn straight to fat. As Professor Terence Stephenson, head of the AMRC, has said, sugary soft drinks are "the ultimate bad food. You are just consuming neat sugar. Your body didn’t evolve to handle this kind of thing.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 报告提出了 10 项建议，其中第一项是在现有 20% 的增值税基础上，对含糖饮料征收 20% 的税至少一年。这至少会是一个很好的开始。软饮料中的糖含量惊人，而且会直接转化为脂肪。正如 AMRC 负责人特伦斯·斯蒂芬森教授所说，含糖软饮料是“终极糟糕的食物。你只是摄入纯糖。你的身体没有进化到能够处理这种事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Precisely. The risks of eating too much fat or salt (which are very different) pale into insignificance compared with the harm done by sugar. And it is everywhere.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 准确地说。与糖所造成的危害相比，摄入过多脂肪或盐（两者截然不同）的风险显得微不足道。它无处不在。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) It is difficult to buy anything in a supermarket, other than plain, unprepared meat, fish or vegetables, that doesn’t have a large amount of sugar in it. This has come about because the prevailing scientific views of the 1960s and 1970s ignored the evidence about sugar, and instead saw fat as the really serious risk, both to the heart and other organs, as well as the cause of obesity.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 除了普通的、未加工的肉、鱼或蔬菜之外，很难在超市买到任何不含大量糖的东西。之所以出现这种情况，是因为 20 世纪 60 年代和 1970 年代盛行的科学观点忽视了有关糖的证据，而是将脂肪视为对心脏和其他器官真正严重的风险，也是肥胖的原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The fashion was to avoid fat. But finding that food with much of its fat removed is not very appetizing, food producers turned to sugar as a magic alternative flavour enhancer, often in the forms of syrups（糖浆）that had recently been developed from com, and put it generously into most prepared foods and soft drinks.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 时尚是避免脂肪。但食品生产商发现去除了大部分脂肪的食物并不是很开胃，于是食品生产商转而使用糖作为一种神奇的替代增味剂，通常以最近从玉米中开发出来的糖浆的形式出现，并将其大量添加到大多数预制食品和软饮料中。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) This stuff is not just fattening. It is addictive. It interferes with the body’s metabolism, possibly via the activity of an appetite-controlling hormone. There’s plenty of evidence for this, for those who will accept the truth.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 这东西不只是增肥。它会让人上瘾。它可能通过控制食欲的激素的活动来干扰身体的新陈代谢。对于那些愿意接受事实的人来说，有大量的证据可以证明这一点。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Theoretically, people ought to make” healthy choices” and avoid overeating. But sugar additives are not easy to identify and are hard to avoid. So the snacking, overdrinking and overeating that makes people fat is not really their own fault：obesity is in large part something that is being done to them. It should be stopped, or rather the government should stop it.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 理论上，人们应该做出“健康的选择”并避免暴饮暴食。但糖类添加剂不易识别且难以避免。因此，吃零食、酗酒和暴饮暴食导致人们发胖，这并不是他们自己的错：肥胖在很大程度上是别人造成的。它应该被制止，或者更确切地说，政府应该制止它。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Going round my local supermarket, I am constantly astonished that it is still legal to sell all the poisons stacked high on the shelves. The problem is that they are worse than useless. They are poisonous. They are known to be addictive. They are known to make people obese. And giving small children sweet drinks or bottles of fake juice all day long is nothing less than child abuse.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 在我当地的超市里，我不断地惊讶于出售货架上高高堆放的所有毒药仍然是合法的。问题是它们比无用更糟糕。它们是有毒的。众所周知，它们会让人上瘾。众所周知，它们会使人肥胖。整天给小孩子喝甜饮料或瓶装假果汁无异于虐待儿童。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Clearly, the sale of such stuff ought to be illegal. I hate to think of yet more government regulation. But a bit of tax on sweet soda and a little more health education, a bit of cooking in schools and banning machines (自动售货机）here and there—as suggested by the AMRC report—is not going to achieve very much. Labelling is quite inadequate. What is needed is legislation banning high levels of sugary syrups used in foods and drinks.
paragraphs.translationZh: N）显然，销售此类东西应该是非法的。我不愿想到更多的政府监管。但是，如 AMRC 报告所建议的那样，对甜汽水征一点税，加强一点健康教育，在学校做一点烹饪，到处禁止自动售货机，效果不会很大。标签还很不充分。我们需要的是立法禁止在食品和饮料中使用高含量的糖浆。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) In June 2012, the then minister for public health said the government was not scared of the food industry and had not ruled out legislation, because of the costs of obesity to the NHS. However, nothing has happened yet. Why not have another Jammie Dodger biscuit and forget about it.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 2012 年 6 月，当时的公共卫生部长表示，政府并不害怕食品工业，也没有排除立法的可能性，因为肥胖会给 NHS 带来成本。然而，还没有发生任何事情。为什么不再吃一块 Jammie Dodger 饼干然后就忘了它呢。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Avoiding over-consumption of sugar can improve peopled health as well as save medical expenses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 避免过度食用糖可以改善人们的健康并节省医疗费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Laws should be passed to make it illegal to produce overly sweet foods or drinks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 应通过法律，将生产过甜食品或饮料定为非法。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Giving small children sweet juices to drink all the time is equal to child abuse.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 一直给小孩子喝甜果汁就等于虐待儿童。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Looking around, the author found obesity quite widespread.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 环顾四周，作者发现肥胖现象相当普遍。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. The number of obese people is expected to increase quickly in the next few decades.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 预计未来几十年肥胖人数将迅速增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. If people really understood the horrible consequences of sugary foods and drinks, they would support government measures against sugar consumption.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 如果人们真正了解含糖食品和饮料的可怕后果，他们就会支持政府针对糖消费的措施。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. It would be a very good beginning to impose an additional tax on sugary drinks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 对含糖饮料征收额外税将是一个非常好的开始。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. The government has not yet taken any action to regulate sugar consumption although it indicated its intention to do so some time ago.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 政府尚未采取任何行动管制食糖消费，但不久前已表示有意这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. Sugar is far more harmful to health than fat and salt.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 糖对健康的危害远远大于脂肪和盐。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. Consumers of sweet foods are not really to blame because they cannot tell what food is sugary.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 甜食的消费者并不是真正的罪魁祸首，因为他们无法分辨什么食物是含糖的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions：There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有2个段落。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The rise of the Internet has been one of the most transformative developments in human history, comparable in impact to the invention of the printing press and the telegraph. Over two billion people worldwide now have access to vastly more information than ever before, and can communicate with each other instantly, often using Web-connected mobile devices they carry everywhere. But the Internets tremendous impact has only just begun.
paragraphs.translationZh: 互联网的兴起是人类历史上最具变革性的发展之一，其影响力可与印刷机和电报的发明相媲美。现在，全世界有超过 20 亿人可以访问比以往更多的信息，并且可以经常使用随身携带的联网移动设备进行即时通信。但互联网的巨大影响才刚刚开始。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Mass adoption of the Internet is driving one of the most exciting social, cultural, and political transformations in history, and unlike earlier periods of change, this time the effects are fully global, ” Schmidt and Cohen write in their new book, The New Digital Age.
paragraphs.translationZh: 施密特和科恩在他们的新书《新数字时代》中写道：“互联网的大规模采用正在推动历史上最激动人心的社会、文化和政治变革之一，与早期的变革不同，这一次的影响是完全全球性的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Perhaps the most profound changes will come when the five billion people worldwide who currently lack Internet access get online. The authors do an excellent job of examining the implications of the Internet revolution for individuals, governments, and institutions like the news media. But if the book has one major shortcoming, it’s that the authors don’t spend enough time applying a critical eye to the role of Internet businesses in these sweeping changes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 也许当全球目前无法访问互联网的 50 亿人上网时，最深刻的变化就会到来。作者出色地研究了互联网革命对个人、政府和新闻媒体等机构的影响。但如果说这本书有一个主要缺点的话，那就是作者没有花足够的时间以批判的眼光来审视互联网企业在这些彻底变革中的作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: In their book, the authors provide the most authoritative volume to date that describes—and more importantly predicts—how the Internet will shape our lives in the coming decades. They paint a picture of a world in which individuals, companies, institutions, and governments must deal with two realities, one physical, and one virtual.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在他们的书中，作者提供了迄今为止最权威的一本书，描述了——更重要的是预测了——互联网将如何在未来几十年塑造我们的生活。他们描绘了这样一个世界：个人、公司、机构和政府必须应对两种现实，一种是物理现实，一种是虚拟现实。

paragraphs.sourceText: At the core of the book is the idea that “technology is neutral, but people aren’t.’’ By using this concept as a starting point, the authors aim to move beyond the now familiar optimist vs. pessimist dichotomy ( 对立观点) that has characterized many recent debates about whether the rise of the Internet will ultimately be good or bad for society. In an interview with TIME earlier this week, Cohen said although he and his co-author are optimistic about many aspects of the Internet, they’ve also realistic about the risks and dangers that lie ahead when the next five billion people come online, particularly with respect to personal privacy and state surveillance (监视).
paragraphs.translationZh: 这本书的核心思想是“技术是中立的，但人不是。”通过使用这个概念作为出发点，作者旨在超越现在熟悉的乐观主义与悲观主义二分法（对立观点），这种二分法是最近关于互联网的崛起最终对社会是好是坏的争论的特征。科恩在本周早些时候接受《时代》杂志采访时表示，尽管他和他的合著者对互联网的许多方面持乐观态度，但他们也对互联网的许多方面持现实态度。接下来的 50 亿人上网时面临的风险和危险，特别是在个人隐私和国家监视 (监视) 方面。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: In 1950, a young man would have found it much easier than it is today to get and keep a job in the auto industry. And in that year the average autoworker could meet monthly mortgage（抵押贷款）payments on an average home with just 13. 4 percent of his take-home pay. Today a similar mortgage would claim more than twice that share of his monthly earnings.
paragraphs.translationZh: 1950 年，年轻人会发现在汽车行业找到并保住一份工作比现在容易得多。在那一年，普通汽车工人仅用其实得工资的 13. 4% 即可支付普通房屋的每月抵押贷款。如今，类似的抵押贷款将占他每月收入的两倍多。

paragraphs.sourceText: Other members of the autoworker’s family, however, might be less inclined to trade the present for the past. His retired parents would certainly have had less economic security back then. Throughout much of the 1960s, more than a quarter of men and women age 65 and older lived below the poverty level, compared to less than 10 percent in 2010.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，汽车工人家庭的其他成员可能不太愿意用现在换过去。那时他退休的父母的经济保障肯定会少一些。在 20 世纪 60 年代的大部分时间里，超过四分之一的 65 岁及以上的男性和女性生活在贫困线以下，而 2010 年这一比例还不到 10%。

paragraphs.sourceText: In most states, his wife could not have taken out a loan or a credit card in her own name. In 42 states, a homemaker had no legal claim on the earnings of her husband. And nowhere did a wife have legal protection against family violence.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在大多数州，他的妻子不能以自己的名义申请贷款或信用卡。在 42 个州，家庭主妇对其丈夫的收入没有合法要求。而且妻子在任何地方都没有受到家庭暴力的法律保护。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most black workers would not want to return to a time when, on average, they earned 40 percent less than their white counterparts (职位相当的人）,while racially restrictive agreements largely prevented them from buying into the suburban neighborhoods being built for white working-class families.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数黑人工人不想回到平均收入比白人工人低 40% 的时代（职位相当的人），而种族限制性协议在很大程度上阻止他们购买为白人工人阶级家庭建造的郊区社区。

paragraphs.sourceText: Today, new problems have emerged in the process of resolving old ones, but the solution is not to go back to the past. Some people may long for an era when divorce was still hard to come by. The spread of no-fault divorce has reduced the bargaining power of whichever spouse is more interested in continuing the relationship. And the breakup of such marriages has caused pain for many families.
paragraphs.translationZh: 今天，在解决老问题的过程中又出现了新问题，但解决办法不是回到过去。有些人可能会向往离婚还很难的时代。无过错离婚的蔓延降低了对继续这段关系更感兴趣的配偶讨价还价的能力。而这样的婚姻破裂，给很多家庭带来了痛苦。

paragraphs.sourceText: The growing diversity of family life comes with new possibilities as well as new challenges. According to a recent poll, more than 80 percent of Americans believe that their current family is as close as the one in which they grew up, or closer. Finding ways to improve the lives of the remaining 20 percent seems more realistic than trying to restore an imaginary golden age.
paragraphs.translationZh: 家庭生活的日益多样化带来了新的可能性和新的挑战。最近的一项民意调查显示，超过 80% 的美国人认为他们现在的家庭与他们长大的家庭一样亲密，甚至更亲密。寻找改善剩下 20% 人生活的方法似乎比试图恢复想象中的黄金时代更为现实。
